title: Particle scale comparator
question: Which displayed scales reuse invariant mass, and which additionally depend on the selected momentum state?
predictionPrompt: Choose one particle and predict which outputs change when its momentum multiplier changes while its catalog mass stays fixed.
sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 adjustment; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
sourceLocator: Electron, muon, proton, and neutron masses; exact h and c; OpenStax sections 5.8-5.9, 6.3, and 6.5; Chapter 8 limits
caveats: Linked axes show dependent representations rather than independent measurements.
The proton and neutron are composite catalog particles; their internal mass structure is not modeled.

numericalMethod.name: Bounded free-particle scale evaluation
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates mass-energy, Compton, de Broglie, and relativistic free-particle identities from one catalog particle and one p/(m c) multiplier.

modelComponents.label: Bounded particle mass catalog
modelComponents.description: Supplies CODATA 2022 invariant masses and elementary/composite labels for electron, muon, proton, and neutron.

attribution.sourceLocator: Electron, muon, proton, and neutron mass entries
caveats: The engine does not propagate mass uncertainties or correlations.

modelComponents.label: Mass-derived scale identities
modelComponents.description: Derives rest energy, mass ratios, and ordinary and reduced Compton wavelengths from the selected invariant mass.

attribution.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 masses; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
attribution.sourceLocator: E_0 = m c^2 and Compton identities using exact h, hbar, and c; OpenStax sections 5.9 and 6.3
caveats: The Compton scale is not a measured particle diameter.

modelComponents.label: Momentum-state scale identities
modelComponents.description: Uses p = k m c to derive de Broglie wavelength and relativistic free-particle total and kinetic energies.

attribution.sourceRevision: SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
attribution.sourceLocator: Exact h and c; OpenStax sections 5.8-5.9 and 6.5; Chapter 8 state-dependency boundary
caveats: Direction, frame comparison, and wave-packet spread are omitted.

equations: E_0 = m c^2; lambda_C = h/(m c); reduced_lambda_C = hbar/(m c)
p = k m c; lambda_dB = h/p
assumptions: The catalog mass is the CODATA 2022 invariant rest mass of a free particle.
The activity exposes only the engine's mass-times-c momentum mode with positive multiplier k from 10^-6 through 10^6.
Momentum is a magnitude in one inertial frame; direction and wave-packet spread are not represented.
The relativistic dispersion relation describes a free particle in vacuum.
Interactions, binding, medium response, finite lifetime, spin, and uncertainty propagation are omitted.

controls.label: Particle
controls.description: Selects one engine catalog particle and its CODATA invariant mass and composition label.
controls.playfulPrompt: Move from the light electron toward the nucleon scale.

controls.label: Momentum divided by m c
controls.description: Sets the positive state momentum as p = k m c within the engine bound.
controls.playfulPrompt: Change momentum without changing the selected invariant mass.

presets.label: Electron at p = m c
presets.description: One valid engine state where the multiplier is one, making electron de Broglie and ordinary Compton wavelengths numerically equal.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Identify which equality comes from the chosen state rather than from a new measurement.

presets.label: Proton at p = m c
presets.description: One composite-particle state using the proton's total invariant mass and no internal-structure model.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Compare its rest and Compton scales with the electron without treating linked axes as independent evidence.

presets.label: Proton at p = 2 m c
presets.description: The same proton catalog mass with twice the p/(m c) multiplier.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Predict which mass-derived outputs stay fixed and which state-derived outputs change.

outputSchema.label: Mass ratio to electron
outputSchema.description: Selected mass divided by electron mass; mass-derived and not an independent observation.

outputSchema.label: Mass ratio to proton
outputSchema.description: Selected mass divided by proton mass; mass-derived and not an independent observation.

outputSchema.label: Rest energy
outputSchema.description: m c^2 derived from the selected mass.

outputSchema.label: Rest energy
outputSchema.description: The same mass-derived rest energy represented in electron volts.

outputSchema.label: Compton wavelength
outputSchema.description: h/(m c), a mass-derived characteristic scale.

outputSchema.label: Reduced Compton wavelength
outputSchema.description: hbar/(m c) = lambda_C/(2 pi), another dependent mass representation.

outputSchema.label: State momentum
outputSchema.description: Positive state momentum k m c selected by the control.

outputSchema.label: de Broglie wavelength
outputSchema.description: h/p, dependent on the selected momentum state.

outputSchema.label: Relativistic total energy
outputSchema.description: Free-particle total energy depending on mass and selected momentum.

outputSchema.label: Relativistic kinetic energy
outputSchema.description: Total energy minus rest energy for the selected state.

outputSchema.label: Particle label
outputSchema.description: Human-readable label for the selected engine catalog particle; composition caveats remain part of the source model contract.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render parallel findings without merging axes or treating differences as empirical residuals when compatibility keys differ.

visualization.description: Shows catalog mass, mass-derived energy and Compton scales, and momentum-state-derived wavelength and energy with dependency labels.

alternatives.description: A sentence names the particle, composition, invariant mass, mass-derived outputs, selected momentum, state-derived outputs, and dependency caveats.
A seven-row table lists quantity, symbol, value, unit, and catalog, mass-derived, or momentum-state-derived dependency.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render final linked-axis markers and dependency labels immediately without animated scale movement.

finding.changed: At runtime, particle choice changes the catalog mass and every dependent scale; momentum multiplier changes only state-dependent momentum, wavelength, and energy outputs.
finding.cause: Rest energy and Compton scales reuse invariant mass, while de Broglie wavelength and relativistic energy additionally reuse selected state momentum.
finding.equation: E_0 = m c^2; lambda_C = h/(m c); lambda_dB = h/p; E^2 = (p c)^2 + (m c^2)^2
assumptions: Positive momentum magnitude p = k m c in one inertial frame
finding.establishes: For an evaluated state, the activity computes explicitly labeled catalog, mass-derived, and momentum-state-derived representations.
finding.doesNotEstablish: Independent measurements of linked outputs, momentum inferred from mass alone, a particle radius, localized wave-packet behavior, composite internal structure, or empirical model validation.
finding.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
finding.sourceLocator: Particle scale equations, dependencies, outputs, OpenStax sections 5.8-5.9, 6.3, and 6.5, and Chapter 8 limits
caveats: Rest energy and Compton scales are mass-derived; de Broglie wavelength is state-dependent.
Joule/electron-volt and ordinary/reduced-Compton pairs are dependent representations, not additional observations.
Composite catalog entries use total invariant mass without an internal constituent model.
No empirical dataset, uncertainty propagation, interaction, or material response is evaluated.
